title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
content:
A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely. The models finish clear, standalone assignments quickly, but they lose track as autonomous developers.

title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
content:
Perplexity is launching a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when relevant changes occur. Its own decision model filters out unimportant results. For Perplexity, the API is part of a broader strategy to stand out from an increasingly interchangeable chatbot business through developer tools.

title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
content:
METR reports that leading AI models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks but getting harder to measure. Current data can't rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development, the organization warns, though it also says common tests may overestimate what the models can actually do.

title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
content:
Security researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to uncover serious vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, finding at least three compromised providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and marketplace resellers who were simply reading customer requests. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and 125 endpoints.

title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
content:
The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct. Dozens of independent verifiers checked the 17 million lines of computer code. The solution arrived years earlier than expected: Terence Tao had predicted it wouldn't happen until around 2050 and didn't expect AI to solve it alone.

title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
content:
TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more.
